why: DEPRECATED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 R10): the node is the parameter receiver, as rclrs's is; use `Node::set_parameter` on the `Node` that `create_node` / `node_mut(id)` returns. Kept one release as a `#[deprecated]` forwarder. PRIOR ROW: phase-426 W2 -- THE writer, and it was missing: `SetParameters` and `SetParametersAtomically` were registered services with no store-side writer any wrapper could reach (`grep -c 'fn set_parameter'` in `nros-node` was 0), so the C facade wrote the slot through `ParameterServer::set` directly. It routes through `ParameterServer::apply`, so an in-image set gets exactly the rules a remote `ros2 param set` gets -- read-only, type, min/max/step, and issue 1151's refusal of an undeclared name. rclcpp's `Node::set_parameter` is the correspondent; the receiver differs for the reason below. phase-426 W1 -- the parameter STORE is one fixed table owned by the EXECUTOR, not a container per node: there is no allocator to make a second, so a node cannot own its own. Upstream's parameter methods are on the node object itself (`rclcpp::Node::declare_parameter`, rclrs's `Node::declare`), which is how upstream keys them; ours are on the executor and the node is an ARGUMENT, because an image composes several nodes onto one executor (RFC-0047) and the shared table has to be told whose parameter it is. The `_on(NodeId, ...)` spelling is the same disambiguation the entity builders already use (`node_mut(id)` / `_on(...)`, phase 104.C). What a user loses: a ported node writes `executor.declare_parameter_on(node_id, name, value)` where rclcpp writes `node->declare_parameter(name, value)`. part of the IMPERATIVE Rust API, which coexists with the declarative component model and is the rclrs-shaped one. Which one `nros::` leads with is settled: rclrs's shape, with `nros::Node` as the one node type and the component model as the `nros::Component` / `nros::DeclarativeNode` extension on top (phase-483; issue 0784, resolved).
